summary: The note describes how countries are building a cybersecurity workforce pipeline through national strategies, addressing a projected skills gap of up to 3.5 million unfilled jobs by 2025. It covers school curricula, public-private partnerships, cyber ranges and competitions, continuous professional development, diversity efforts, and international collaboration, with dated milestones from September 2023 to March 2024.
one_line: Nations are building cybersecurity talent pipelines via education, industry partnerships, cyber ranges, ongoing training, diversity initiatives, and international cooperation to close a large skills gap.
key_facts: On September 7, 2023, at the International Cybersecurity Symposium, Jessica Reed reported that by 2025 there could be as many as 3.5 million unfilled cybersecurity jobs globally.
On October 15, 2023, the Ministry of Education, in collaboration with cybersecurity expert Alex Johnson, decided to introduce foundational cybersecurity modules in high school programs nationwide.
The high school cybersecurity modules aim to instill basic cyber hygiene, encourage logical problem-solving, and spark interest in the profession, not make every student a specialist.
On November 22, 2023, several top technology companies announced partnerships with public education systems to link classroom theory with practical industry skills.
Public-private partnerships include internship programs, tech talks, and mentorship opportunities for students.
On December 10, 2023, the Cyber Defence Alliance announced the launch of a national cyber range, spearheaded by figures such as Dr. Emily Thompson.
Cyber ranges are simulated environments where aspiring professionals practice defending against mock cyberattacks.
Cybersecurity competitions such as 'Capture The Flag' (CTF) events and hackathons serve both talent discovery and educational purposes.
On January 3, 2024, online platforms and universities announced advanced cybersecurity courses and certificates providing a progression path for every level of expertise.

On February 20, 2024, industry leaders at the Cyber Diversity Summit discussed increasing participation of women, minorities, and other underrepresented groups, concluding diverse perspectives offer a strategic advantage.
On March 7, 2024, an international cybersecurity training initiative was launched among various countries to share expertise, tactics, and best practices.
Several countries have created cybersecurity awareness programs for the entire workforce, not just IT professionals.
